## Zoning & Development Analysis: 6247 N Rockwell St

**PIN:** 13012120030000 | **Parcel Resolution:** Authoritative (PIN confirmed from county address records)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-2 (Residential Single-Unit District)**. RS-2 is one of three RS sub-districts differentiated primarily by minimum lot area requirements and floor area ratios [5]. You can verify this on the official Chicago Zoning Map at [https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

**Confidence:** High — sourced from the city's authoritative GIS parcel database.

---

### 2. Can You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Almost certainly not as-of-right under RS-2**, but there is one narrow exception worth examining.

RS districts — including RS-2 — are intended primarily for detached single-family houses on individual lots [5]. Two-flats and multi-unit buildings are the domain of RT, RM, and higher districts [5].

The one exception in the code applies to **RS-3** (not RS-2): [1] provides that in RS-3, the minimum lot area per unit *may* be reduced to 1,500 sq ft for a two-unit building when 60% or more of the zoning lots on the same block face are already improved with multi-unit buildings, or when the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries [1]. **This exemption expressly applies to RS-3 only**, so it would not benefit an RS-2 parcel.

To build a two-flat, you would most likely need a **rezoning to RT or RM**, which is a legislative process through the Zoning Board of Appeals and City Council.

**Confidence:** High on the baseline restriction. The rezoning path involves political and procedural factors that cannot be assessed from data alone.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards (RS-2)

The context did not return the full RS-2 zone definition table, so I can state what the Municipal Code and property record establish, with the caveat that the complete standards table should be confirmed directly in the ordinance or with CDPD:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** RS-2 requires a larger minimum lot area per dwelling unit than RS-3; the exact RS-2 figure is governed by [1], but the specific square-footage threshold for RS-2 was not returned in the data — verify in [1] and the full RS-2 bulk table at § 17-2-0303.
- **FAR and height limits:** The RS-2 district standards are set out in § 17-2-0300 generally [1], but the specific FAR and maximum height numbers for RS-2 were not in the returned code chunks — confirm via the zoning map link above or the [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoning_ordinance.html).
- **This parcel's physical dimensions:** The lot is **4,125 sq ft** (per Cook County Assessor), and the existing building is a 1-story, 1,661 sq ft masonry structure built in 1925 with a full basement.
- **Off-street parking location:** In RS districts, off-street parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line; parking may access a required side setback only via a permitted driveway from the front [2].
- **Setbacks:** General setback standards for RS-2 are in § 17-2-0400 (not returned in context) — verify directly.

**Confidence:** Moderate — the code framework is confirmed, but specific numerical thresholds (FAR, height, exact min lot area) for RS-2 require direct ordinance lookup.

### 5. Parking Requirements and Transit Reductions

In RS districts, required off-street parking for residential uses must be located **on the same zoning lot** as the dwelling units served [2]. Parking is not permitted in side setbacks except when accessed by a driveway from the front property line, and is prohibited within 20 feet of the front property line [2].

The specific *number* of required spaces for RS-2 (typically 1 space per dwelling unit for single-family) is set in § 17-10-0100 et seq. (not returned in context) — verify directly.

**TOD parking reductions:** Because this parcel is **not in a TOD area**, the Connected Communities Ordinance parking reductions do not apply. The nearest transit (Metra at 1.04 miles) does not bring this parcel within the TOD threshold.

**Confidence:** High on the location/access rules [2]; moderate on the specific number of required spaces (requires direct code lookup).

---

### 6. Coach House / ADU

**This is where the answer is clear and somewhat restrictive.**

[4] establishes "Additional Dwelling Unit-Allowed RS Areas" — designated areas where coach houses and conversion units may be legally developed in single-family zones. A building permit for a new coach house unit **may not be issued for any RS-designated zoning lot unless it complies with [4]** (§ 17-7-0570), which requires the lot to be within a designated ADU-Allowed Area [3].

**This parcel is confirmed NOT in an ADU-Allowed Area.** Therefore, a new coach house cannot be permitted as-of-right.

If the parcel *were* in an ADU area, the applicable rules would include [3]:
- Coach houses may not exceed **22 feet** in building height
- Rooftop features capped at 22 feet above grade
- At least **3 feet of open space** unobstructed from ground to sky must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line for the entire building wall length (except where a side line abuts an alley or street)
- Coach houses may be established without accessory parking to serve the coach house itself [3]
